description: Run a wasmQ envelope (wai.quantum.wasmq/1 or /2, extensions/quantum-wasmq.md): an OpenQASM 3 program and the WebAssembly modules its `extern`s call between gates, in one content-addressed envelope. The quantum part is simulated here (the stabilizer tableau, or the second version's whole-number state vector for t, Toffoli and dyadic angles), each callout a metered call of its module; the run is the same bytes on every host and engine. The job gives the counts, the calls and the fuel each used, the modules' digests, the digest of every call, and the fault that stopped the run if one did (a fault is sealed, not an error). A second-version run's energy is what the service read of the worker that ran it: the process's CPU energy on macOS, the processor packages' over its window on Linux, or the unmetered form with the reason where the host reads none, never zero; the first version states only that it is unmetered. The run is a job: past the answer's wait its id comes back to poll with get_quantum_job, and an envelope past what the service takes is refused, naming the local command. Sealed with the service's key; verify_quantum_receipt holds the job to the profile's form (section 6.5). Give the envelope as base64, or name an example; an envelope the profile refuses is refused with its code (W001 to W017).

envelope_base64.description: The envelope (a WAI1 file of capability wai.quantum.wasmq, as `wai-quantum pack-wasmq` writes it), as standard base64.

example.description: One of the profile's own envelopes instead: the surface-code round decoded in the middle of the circuit, the atom planner, a fault sealed, and the second version's exact method, feedback, angle arguments and rotations.

name: run_wasmq

digests.description: The BLAKE3 digests the store keeps the job's objects under: its request, its program (a wasmQ run's envelope, under the digest its receipt binds), its result and its receipt.

error.description: Why the job failed: a worker stopped past its admitted memory or the job's time says so, and nothing is sealed.

estimate.description: The plan's memory, bytes, and its work: §4.8's operations for a wasmQ run, amplitudes touched for a qudit job.

anyOf.description: The run's result (section 6.4): its outcome, the counts of its shots, its calls and the fuel they used, the modules' digests, the digest of every call, the accuracy, the energy, and the receipt.

callouts.description: The calls into the modules that returned.

counts.description: Each outcome and how often it came, keyed by the program's bits with the highest first.

energy.description: The first version: exactly {"unmetered": why}. The second (section 11.5): {"run", "callouts"}, the run's figure (a reading where the host meters it, the unmetered form with why where it does not, never zero) and each callout's (the unmetered form: no meter resolves one call).

fault.description: Where the run stopped and why (section 6.2): its reason, its shot, its phase, the module, the fuel used, and the callout and budget where they apply.

budget.description: The budget that ran out, where one did.

fuel.description: The fuel the stopped call or instance used.

phase.description: Where in the shot it stopped: a call, or an instance's seed, prior or init.

fuel.description: The fuel used, in all and in the instances' seeds, priors and init; the budgets; and each callout's calls, fuel and most in one call.

blake3.description: A BLAKE3 digest, 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits.

receipt.description: The job receipt every job takes (receipt.v2.json).

shots_run.description: The shots that ended: all of them, or those before the fault.

status.description: ok: every shot ran; fault: the run stopped, and fault says where and why.

anyOf.description: A BLAKE3 digest, 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits.

transcript_blake3.description: The digest of every call's inputs, outputs and fuel, in order, for a run that ended ok; null for one that faulted.

anyOf.description: A program run (wai-quantum qudit run): the counts, the amplitudes asked for, the state's digest and norm, the constants' digest, the work and the accuracy.

accuracy.description: bit-exact: the same integers on every host; bound is the 2-norm distance from the ideal state at most (bound_units in units of 2^-30), and outcomes the total variation between the law the counts are drawn from and the ideal outcome distribution at most (quantum-sim.md section 9.4).

amplitudes.description: Each amplitude asked for, by its digits: the integers it is at 2^-30.

constants.description: The digest of every constant the dimension's gates read: its roots of unity and its Fourier entries (quantum-sim.md section 9.2).

blake3.description: A BLAKE3 digest, 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits.

counts.description: Each outcome drawn and how often, keyed by the qudits' digits with the highest qudit first; at most 65536 outcomes are listed, the most frequent first.

d.description: The register's dimension: the levels of each qudit.

service_kwh.description: A provider job: the provider's own figure.

attribution.description: Whose energy it is: the job's worker process, or none (the processor packages' over the job's window, every process on the host in it).

concurrent_jobs.description: Other jobs that ran on the host during the window.

counter.description: The package counter as seen: the longest it went between updates, and the smallest step it took.

declared.description: What the stated uncertainty covers, and what it does not.

energy.description: The CPU energy of the job's process as the kernel counts it, with its uncertainty and what it leaves out, or unmetered with the reason.

engine.description: The engine that made the result: the wai-quantum crate's name and version.

gates.description: How many gates the program holds.

omitted_shots.description: The shots of the outcomes not listed.

receipt.description: A result's receipt: an Ed25519 signature, by the key it names, over digest = BLAKE3("wai:quantum-service-receipt\x02" ‖ len ‖ request ‖ len ‖ result), each of request and result in its RFC 8785 canonical text (the result without its receipt member), each length 8 bytes big-endian. Whatever members the request and the result hold are sealed, the result's engine and schema among them. The first receipts (no canon member, $defs/first) sealed their writer's compact text under the domain ending \x01; they still verify. wai/extensions/quantum-providers.md section 8.2 states the seal in full, and section 8.4 what a verifier checks.

canon.description: The canonical form the digest is taken over.

digest.description: The digest signed, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

key.description: The signing key, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

signature.description: The signature, 64 bytes in lower-case hex.

time.description: When the receipt was issued and, where it states one, until when it is offered, by the signer's clock, in milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Absent on a receipt that seals no time (one from a host with no clock, or sealed before receipts stated one). With it, the digest is taken under the domain ending \x03 and ends with len ‖ the canonical text of this member, so the time cannot be changed or taken off (section 8.2).

not_after_ms.description: The first moment the receipt is no longer offered: after issued_ms.

receipt.title: wai.quantum.receipt/2

state.description: The final state: its BLAKE3 (quantum-sim.md section 9.6), its amplitudes, and the sum of their squared moduli at 2^-30.

blake3.description: A BLAKE3 digest, 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits.

verdict.description: For a job that gave an intent: the engine's verdict of its counts, sealed with them.

critique.description: The program's smells, each with its lines.

executed.description: The method that ran and its accuracy class, and the distance a compile put between the program and what ran.

items.description: One intent's check: what it asked, whether it held, how strong the check was, how it was made, the layer it stands on and that layer's limits.

distribution.description: The program's distribution, when its outcomes are few enough to list.

expected.description: An expectation intent: the value the intent states.

fit.description: A sampled intent: the test, its statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value, the level, and whether it rejected.

impossible.description: The outcomes sampled that the stated distribution gives probability 0: the first 64, in order.

impossible_outcomes.description: How many outcomes sampled the stated distribution gives probability 0.

layer.description: The layer the check stands on: unchecked when it was not decided.

limits.description: What that layer does not show.

method.description: A sampled intent: the method the samples were run by.

outcomes.description: The outcomes the distribution holds, or the samples' distinct outcomes.

outside.description: An outcomes or a conserves intent: how much lies outside, as probability of the exact distribution or as a fraction of the samples.

said.description: An energy-landscape job's own word: solved, missed, failed or unchecked.

samples.description: An outcomes or a conserves intent checked on the job's counts: how many samples.

value.description: An expectation intent: the observable's exact value on the program's state.

layer.description: The layer that decided the intents: the weakest of the checks' layers, and unchecked when an intent was not decided or none was given. Absent from a verdict sealed before layers were named.

limits.description: What that layer does not show.

parsed.description: Whether the reader took the program, and its warnings and notes with their codes, or its refusal.

items.description: One of the reader's diagnostics: its code, what happens to the construct it is about, its message (without the line or the code), and where it stands.

text.description: The refusal as the reader wrote it, with its line and code.

rank.description: The level's place on the ladder, from 0 (refused) to 4 (proof).

refusal.description: For a refused job: its message and its codes.

repairs.description: Each edit a repair made, with the code it answered and the lines it changed.

statement.description: The level in one plain line.

verdict.title: wai.quantum.verdict/1

work.description: Amplitudes touched: each gate's, the register walked for the draws and the hash, and the shots.

why.description: What the plan read of it: the profile, the method, the qubits or the register, the shots and the work.

anyOf.description: A refusal as data: the message, every code in it (the last is the code), its outcome and meaning as the code's table gives them. A host that refuses for its own reasons gives the error alone.

A wasmQ envelope's or a qudit job's job (run_wasmq, run_qudit; POST /v1/wasmq, POST /v1/qudit): queued, running, done with its result and receipt, or failed with its error; or the refusal. Its request is what the receipt binds: for a wasmQ run the contract and the envelope's digest, for a qudit job the request as given.
